metadata.match: Vancouver Regional Qualifier Day 2 Finals BO3

title: Diana vs Rengar: the three-game finals lesson in bounce, hidden answers, and counter-pressure
summary: The Vancouver finals should be studied as a full best-of-three. Game 1 shows Rengar breaking through early Vex pressure. Game 2 shows Diana sideboard into Singularity and hide Hard Bargain through Stacked Deck. Game 3 turns Kai'Sa, Thrill of the Hunt, and Pyke into a sequence of Moonfall, Hard Bargain, Star-Crossed, Traveling Merchant, and Tideturner.

sections.heading: Diana's series lesson
body: Game 1 is the warning: early Vex pressure is not enough if Rengar can clear it and keep a second battlefield live.
Game 2 is the adaptation: Singularity from the sideboard and hidden Hard Bargain change Rengar's planning rules.
Game 3 is the finish: Diana does not simply topdeck Tideturner; Moonfall, Hard Bargain, and Star-Crossed keep the board meaningful for that draw.

sections.heading: Six practice clips for the whole match

clips.lesson: Diana opens Game 1 on Ravenbloom Conservatory, but still needs a second layer behind Vex.
Rengar clears early Vex and exposes Diana's first defensive layer.
Singularity turns Rengar's midgame board into a resource exchange.
Stacked Deck hides Hard Bargain and ties the series.
Hard Bargain stops the first Thrill of the Hunt line in Game 3.
Star-Crossed changes the last battlefield and opens the door for Traveling Merchant into Tideturner.

sections.heading: Diana deck context
body: Diana wins by repeatedly changing how the final turns resolve, not by passively stalling.
Ravenbloom Conservatory, Targon's Peak, and Abandoned Hall give different ways to buy one more turn.
Singularity and hidden Hard Bargain are the sideboard and information tools that reshape Games 2 and 3.

sections.heading: Game 1: early Vex is not enough by itself
breakdown: Starting condition: Diana opens on Ravenbloom Conservatory with Vex and interaction.
Turning point: Rengar clears Vex and prevents the control unit from becoming a long-term engine.
Replay standard: before committing Vex, Diana should ask what second layer punishes an immediate answer.
timeline: 04:36:08 Rengar closes through a second battlefield

sections.heading: Game 2: sideboard cards and hidden information tie the match
breakdown: Starting condition: Sabotage reveals Singularity, Gust, Ravenbloom Student, and Stupefy.
Turning point: Singularity handles the midgame board and prevents Rengar from racing cleanly.
Replay standard: Stacked Deck should hide the answer until the turn Rengar most wants to commit.

sections.heading: Game 3: the championship point is built before Tideturner
breakdown: Starting condition: both players know the sideboard pattern, so Diana must split answers across Kai'Sa, Thrill of the Hunt, and Pyke.
Turning point: Moonfall, Hard Bargain, and Star-Crossed keep downgrading Rengar's closing lines.
Replay standard: count the board twice, before bounce and after bounce, before treating any final turn as safe.
timeline: 05:29:30 Hard Bargain stops Thrill of the Hunt

sections.heading: Diana practice checklist
body: Protect or replace early Vex instead of relying on it as a single defensive layer.
Write Singularity, Hard Bargain, and Moonfall into the post-sideboard curve.
Use Stacked Deck to protect hidden interaction, not just to gain value.
keyRules: Vex: play her when the second defensive layer is ready.
Singularity: hold for the turn when Rengar's midgame units enter the same answer window.
Stacked Deck plus Hard Bargain: hide the counter until the Rengar player must commit.
Moonfall and Star-Crossed: change the location and resource math of the final attack.
Traveling Merchant plus Tideturner: only works because earlier turns preserved a meaningful board.

sections.heading: Diana mistakes to avoid
body: Treating Game 1 Vex as an automatic win condition.
Using Stacked Deck too early and losing hidden-answer value.
Remembering Game 3 as only a Tideturner topdeck instead of a sequence of setup turns.

sections.heading: Rengar's series lesson
body: Game 1 is the model: remove Vex early, preserve multiple battlefields, and close at reaction speed.
Game 2 shows the danger of assuming Sabotage gives perfect information; Stacked Deck and face-down answers still matter.
Game 3 shows why Thrill of the Hunt needs a second path. If one bounce spell or one counterspell can reset the turn, Diana gets time to redraw.

clips.lesson: Clearing Vex is the start of Rengar's winning Game 1 structure.
Reaction timing and a second battlefield close Game 1.
Sabotage gives visible information, not complete information.
Hidden Hard Bargain punishes a single-line final push.
Kai'Sa being answered means Rengar needs a second pressure line immediately.
Thrill of the Hunt must be backed by another battlefield.

sections.heading: Rengar deck context
body: Rengar is strongest when it makes Diana answer hand information, battlefield position, and reaction timing at once.
Sabotage is a planning tool, not a guarantee against face-down answers.
Thrill of the Hunt should close an already split board, not become the only test.

sections.heading: Game 1: the correct Rengar template
breakdown: Starting condition: Diana opens on Ravenbloom Conservatory, so Rengar must deny the value engine.
Turning point: clearing Vex lets Rengar preserve a second battlefield.
Replay standard: after clearing Vex, Rengar should still have another scoring point, not just a temporary board.

sections.heading: Game 2: visible information is not full information
breakdown: Starting condition: Sabotage sees part of Diana's hand.
Turning point: Singularity and hidden Hard Bargain make the endgame unsafe.
Replay standard: before committing, ask whether a face-down Hard Bargain still leaves a second battlefield.
timeline: 05:09:34 Hard Bargain breaks the final push

sections.heading: Game 3: do not leave only one Thrill of the Hunt line
breakdown: Starting condition: Diana has already shown bounce and counters, so Rengar must expect them.
Turning point: Kai'Sa, Thrill of the Hunt, and Pyke are answered one at a time.
Replay standard: every big push needs a second battlefield or a follow-up threat after bounce.
timeline: 05:29:30 Thrill of the Hunt is stopped
05:37:03 Diana gets time to find Tideturner

sections.heading: Rengar practice checklist
body: Clear Diana's control units before racing.
Treat face-down cards and Stacked Deck as real information problems.
Make Thrill of the Hunt a multi-line closer, not a single-card test.
keyRules: Sabotage: use before committing key midgame threats, but keep planning for unknown cards.
Kai'Sa: play when Diana cannot fold her into the same Singularity or Moonfall window.
Thrill of the Hunt: only commit when bounce or Hard Bargain does not end the entire turn.
Punch First and Irresistible Faefolk: compress Diana's defensive turns instead of only chasing immediate points.
Determined Sentry and Pyke: force Diana to answer more than one battlefield.

sections.heading: Rengar mistakes to avoid
body: Assuming Game 1 pressure will still work after Diana sideboards.
Treating Sabotage as complete information.
Letting the final turn become a single bounce-or-counter test.
